title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
statement: You are given an unsorted list of integers nums, which may contain duplicates. A run is a set of distinct integer values v, v+1, v+2, ..., v+k that are all present somewhere in nums (their positions in the list do not matter). Return the length of the longest such run, counting each value once no matter how many times it appears. For example, [12, 300, 15, 11, 14, 200, 13] contains the run 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, so the answer is 5. Return 0 for an empty list; a non-empty list always has an answer of at least 1. Your solution must run in O(n) expected time, so sorting is off the table — use a hash set.
hints: Sorting gives O(n log n). What data structure lets you ask 'is the value x present?' in O(1) so you can walk a run without sorting?
Put every value in a hash set. A value v is the left edge of a run exactly when v - 1 is NOT in the set — only start counting from those edges, so each value is visited O(1) times overall.

Build values = set(nums). For each v in the set, if v - 1 not in values, walk upward: length = 1; while v + length in values: length += 1. Track the max length; duplicates vanish automatically because the set stores each value once.
